title: This Bird Dives at 242 Miles an Hour (Fastest Animal on Earth)

scenes.text: This bird dives at 242 miles an hour.
The peregrine falcon. The fastest animal on Earth, by a mile.
It climbs high, folds its wings, and drops like a missile straight onto a pigeon.
It strikes with its feet, so hard the prey is knocked out of the sky before it ever bites.
At that speed the air would be too much to breathe. Its nostrils have tiny bony cones that slow the air down.
scenes.keywords: peregrine falcon face close up beak

scenes.text: 242 miles an hour. A bird did that.

description:
A peregrine falcon has been clocked diving at 242 miles an hour, the fastest speed ever recorded for any animal.
The record was set by a falcon named Frightful, released from a plane and tracked with a skydiver's altimeter. Peregrines climb high, fold their wings and strike prey with their feet mid-air; small bony cones in their nostrils help them breathe at that speed.
What's the fastest thing you've ever seen move? Comment below.
first_comment: A cheetah tops out around 60 to 70 mph on the ground. The falcon does almost four times that in a dive. Which would win a race: falcon or fighter jet on takeoff?
